question: On 26 February 2024, the Spanish national newspaper El País published an article1 stating that the EU Intelligence and Situation Centre (EU INTCEN) had produced an intelligence report alleging Russian involvement in supporting the Catalan independence movement. This report was said to have been drafted in November 2017.

In September 2021, The New York Times also referred to a report that may have been produced by EU INTCEN. However, in response to our inquiry E-004166/20212, the EEAS informed us that ‘EU INTCEN intelligence assessments are mainly based on the strategic intelligence assessments of EU Member States’ and that EU INTCEN was ‘not the author of the report mentioned in the article’.

On 6 February 2024, Commission Vice-President Schinas stated in Parliament that there were reports of frequent and close contacts between Russian officials and representatives of a Catalan secessionist group between 2017 and 2020. We raised question P-000419/20243 regarding this issue, which has still not been answered. 1.
Did EU INTCEN draft the report mentioned in El País?
If so, did EU INTCEN produce the report on its own initiative, or upon the request of the VP/HR or another EU institution?
Is the report mentioned in El País the same one as that mentioned in The New York Times?

Vice-President for ‘Promoting our European Way of Life’ in his plenary intervention of 6 February 2024 drew attention to the available sources that state this evidence, including Parliament resolutions.

In its resolutions of 9 March 2022 (8) and 13 July 2023 (9), the Parliament asked for in-depth investigation of ‘findings about the close and regular contacts between Russian officials and representatives of a group of Catalan secessionists in Spain’ […]’ calling them ‘part of Russia’s wider strategy to use each and every opportunity to manipulate discourse in order to promote destabilisation’.

The Parliament also expressed ‘concerns about Russia’s connections with several political parties and politicians in the EU and its wide-ranging interference with secessionist movements in European territories and in the EU, such as in Catalonia’ in its resolution of 1 June 2023 (10).

The issue is also addressed in the Parliament’s most recent resolution of 8 February 2024 (11), which refers to numerous reports highlighting contacts and close personal relationships between secessionists in Catalonia, including authorities of the government of the autonomous community of Catalonia and the Kremlin, and expresses extreme concerns about these allegations.

The EU Intelligence and Situation Centre (EU INTCEN) provides strategic intelligence on early warning, situational awareness, strategic foresight and threat assessments to support the various EU decision-making bodies. EU INTCEN intelligence assessments are mainly based on the strategic intelligence assessments of Member States’ intelligence and security services.
The Commission does not have any comments on reports mentioned in the press.
